articles.summary: Having a TFSA, RRSP and taxable investment account can make investing feel more complicated than it needs to be. You might wonder what should go in each account, whether they should all hold the same investments, or which account you should add money to next. A simpler place to start is with one question: What are you using the money for?
articles.title: How to manage a TFSA, RRSP and taxable account together in Canada

articles.summary: Your investment plan should still fit what you want the money for today. Big life changes are a good reason to check whether your old plan still makes sense. You do not need to change anything just because markets move or the news is scary.
articles.title: Your portfolio can be on target and still be wrong for your life

articles.summary: Your first $1,000 does not need a complicated investment strategy. The most important decision happens before you choose what to invest in. What you do with the next $1,000 matters more than finding a “perfect” first investment.
articles.title: How to invest your first $1,000 in Canada
